info.description: WhoisBase looks domains up live at the registry and says so honestly. RDAP is resolved through the IANA bootstrap (data.iana.org) to the TLD's authoritative registry server, and TLDs with no RDAP endpoint (.at, .rs, .eu, .de, .io, .ch) are queried live on the registry's own port-43 whois server - the TLDs other whois APIs return blank. Records are cached for at most 300 seconds, and every response carries a cache block with the record's age, so you always know how fresh your answer is; pass fresh=true (or force=1) and the cache is genuinely bypassed and the registry is re-asked before you get an answer. An unregistered domain returns registered: false with the full record schema instead of blank fields, and every failure - timeout, rate limit, unreachable registry - is a structured JSON error that names the problem, never a bare 504 or an empty 200. Domain availability is built in: /availability promotes the unregistered answer to a first-class result with the registry source named, /availability/bulk checks up to 50 domains in one call (each domain counts as one request), /dns returns live DNS records with TTLs as returned, and /suggest lists only name variants verified available against the registry - never unverified guesses. Premium status is reported only when a registry itself publishes it.
